topics.label: Course introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the session by connecting histopathology practical observations to the lecture's learning outcomes on cellular transformation and cancer genetics.

topics.label: Discovery of cellular oncogenes from tumor viruses and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how tumor virology led to the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes and describe the laboratory assays used to test cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification, cell cycle regulation, and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes and explain how their mutations disrupt cell cycle checkpoints and cellular phenotypes through dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative mechanisms.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinctions between sequence and chromosomal instability, detailing how specific defects in DNA repair, replication proofreading, and mitotic chromosome segregation cause genomic damage.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression, hereditary predisposition, and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sequential mutations drive cancer progression in multi-step models, how germline mutations accelerate cancer development in hereditary syndromes, and how tumors adapt and evolve.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the lecture by reviewing learning outcomes, inviting questions, and offering recommended reading for the upcoming break.
